title: Restocking Timing Points: Delivery to First Carrier Scan
content:
Timing points weigh how promptly a parcel went back. For grade B units on a Returns & Exchanges return, they move the restocking percentage by the calendar days from the order's delivered date to the parcel's first carrier scan.

## Timing points

| Days from delivered date to first carrier scan | Timing points |
|---|---|
| More than 30 | Adds 5 percentage points |
| 11 to 30 | None |
| 10 or fewer | Takes off 3 percentage points |

The restocking percentage so moved is never below zero.

## Both sides of each threshold

| Days | Points |
|---|---|
| 10 | Takes off 3 |
| 11 | None |
| 30 | None |
| 31 | Adds 5 |

The delivered date is read from the Online Orders record of the order and the first carrier scan date from the return.

Example (hypothetical): with a restocking percentage of 15 percent, a parcel first scanned 8 days after delivery is charged at 12 percent; one first scanned 35 days after delivery, at 20 percent.
